 2   Q1.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME, BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A.    My name is Enedina Soto. My business address is 100 North Stanton Street,

 4         El Paso, Texas, 79901.

 5

 6   Q2.   ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU SUBMITTING THIS TESTIMONY

 7   A.    I am filing this testimony on behalf of El Paso Electric Company (“EPE” or “the

 8         Company”).

 9

10   Q3.   HAVE YOU PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED TESTIMONY IN THIS

11         PROCEEDING?

12   A.    Yes. I submitted Direct Testimony in this proceeding on March 27, 2026.

13

14            II.     PURPOSE OF SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY

15   Q4.   WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT

16         TESTIMONY?

17   A.    The purpose of my Supplemental Direct Testimony is to respond to Pre-Hearing

18         Bench Request Paragraph 9.o.

19

 3   Q5.   WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.o OF

4          THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

 5   A.    Paragraph 9.o of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “…the specific

 6         percentage changes in cost allocation for New Mexico retail, Texas retail, and

 7         wholesale jurisdictions from the Historical Test Year, and what is the detailed

 8         breakdown of the load driving these changes in the New Mexico retail

 9         jurisdiction?”

10

11   Q6.   IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.o., WHAT ARE THE SPECIFIC

12         PERCENTAGE CHANGES IN COST ALLOCATION FOR NEW MEXICO

13         RETAIL, TEXAS RETAIL, AND WHOLESALE JURISDICTIONS FROM

14         HISTORICAL TEST YEAR?

15   A.    EPE is interpreting this question to request the changes to the jurisdictional

16         allocation factors from the Base Period to the Historical Test Year used in EPE’s

17         rate application. These changes are shown in Table ES-1S. Detailed calculations

18         are shown in Exhibit ES-1S. The adjustments for dedicated resources are discussed

19         in the direct testimony of EPE witness Enedina Soto.

20

10   Q7.   IN FURTHER RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.o, WHAT IS THE

11         DETAILED BREAKDOWN OF THE LOAD DRIVING THESE CHANGES

12         IN THE NEW MEXICO RETAIL JURISDICTION?

13   A.    The detailed breakdown of the difference in energy and demand between the

14         Historical Test Year Period and the Base Period for each rate class are shown in

15         Exhibit ES-2S. Energy for the Historical Test Year Period reflects adjustments for

16         energy efficiency, year-end customer annualization, and weather.            These

17         adjustments are detailed in Exhibit RFG-01 included with the direct testimony of

18         EPE witness Rene Gonzalez. The adjusted energy values are used to derive

19         Historical Test Year demand; therefore, these adjustments are already reflected in

20         the Historical Test Year demand.



                                               3

1         In addition, there are also differences in the dedicated resource adjustments that

2         drive the changes in load between the Historical Test Year Period and the Base

3         Period. These differences are also shown in Exhibit ES-2S.

4

5   Q8.   DOES      THIS     CONCLUDE          YOUR       SUPPLEMENTAL            DIRECT

6         TESTIMONY?

7   A.    Yes.

1
  The adjustment for dedicated resources for the Historical Test Year Period differs from the Base Period adjustment because EPE annualizes the generation for each facility. This is done by calculating a capacity factor to estimate expected generation at the time of the system peak, whereas the
Base Period data reflects actual observed generation for each resource.
2
  The adjustment for the Carne facility was included in the Historical Test Year Period because the facility is expected to come online by the time the new rates are in effect
3
    The adjustment for the Santa Teresa facility was included in the Historical Test Year Period because the facility is expected to come online by the time the new rates are in effect
4
    During the Base Period, generation from the Milagro facility was temporarily reassigned towards meeting 2025 NM RPS requirements. Accordingly, only the Base Period includes a reduction in NM load to account for this.

          1.     I affirm in writing under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of

New Mexico that the following statements are true and correct.

          2.     I am over 18 years of age and have personal knowledge of the facts stated herein.

I am employed by El Paso Electric Company ("EPE" or “the Company”) as the Manager of Load

Research and Data Analytics.

          3.     The foregoing Supplemental Direct Testimony of Enedina Soto, together with all

exhibits sponsored therein and attached thereto, is true and accurate based on my knowledge and

belief.

          4.     I submit this Declaration, based upon my personal knowledge and upon information

and belief, in support of EPE’s Application for Revisions of Its Retail Electric Rates Pursuant to

Advice Notice No. 317.
